title: Claude-Ported GPU Number Field Sieve Factors 270-Digit RSA-896 Challenge
aiSystem: Anthropic Claude (CADO-NFS GPU Port & Fleet Orchestration)
whyItMatters: Stephen A. Weis used Claude to port CADO-NFS to GPUs and orchestrate 2,048 H100s, factoring the 270-digit RSA-896 challenge number—setting a new public 896-bit integer factoring record.
summary: On September 19, 2026, Anthropic researcher Stephen A. Weis published the exact prime factorization of RSA-896, a 270-decimal-digit (896-bit) RSA Factoring Challenge modulus open since 1991. Using Claude to port the CADO-NFS General Number Field Sieve pipeline to NVIDIA H100 GPUs and orchestrate preemptible execution across up to 2,048 idle GPUs, the computation sieved 1.774 billion special-q lattices, gathered 29.08 billion unique relations, and solved a 1.48-billion-row sparse matrix in 10.07 calendar days (~30 GPU-years), extending the public factoring frontier from 862 to 896 bits.
technicalHighlights: Published exact 135-digit prime factors p and q multiplying identically to the 270-digit RSA-896 challenge modulus (trivially and unconditionally verifiable).
Claude ported CADO-NFS sieving and ECM cofactorization to H100 GPUs and orchestrated distributed runs across up to 256 preemptible 8-GPU nodes over 10.07 calendar days.
Extended the public integer factorization record from RSA-260 (862 bits) to 896 bits, demonstrating practical vulnerability of legacy RSA-1024 to GPU data-center fleets.
caveats: Does not improve the asymptotic complexity of the General Number Field Sieve (GNFS) and poses no threat to RSA-2048 or larger keys; represents an AI-accelerated HPC engineering and systems breakthrough rather than a new factoring algorithm.

scoreRationale.foundational: Sets a landmark 896-bit public integer factoring record on a 35-year-old RSA Factoring Challenge target.
scoreRationale.ripple: Demonstrates that AI-assisted GPU porting and orchestration bring legacy RSA-1024 well within reach of modern AI data centers.
scoreRationale.verification: Exact prime factors p and q are publicly posted and unconditionally verified in milliseconds by integer multiplication and primality testing.
scoreRationale.velocity: Completed a world-record 896-bit GNFS factorization in 10.07 calendar days using AI-ported GPU code on idle cluster capacity.
